title: Adages & Puns
blurb: Two skills — sayings that teach a lesson, and words doing two jobs at once — then one full-topic proof.

core.title: Adages
core.skill: What an adage means, and how the story around it tells you

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions. The sentences are numbered.
sentences: Mina spent three weeks building a volcano for the science fair.
She painted it gray and added fake lava with glue and glitter gel.
The night before the competition, she proudly placed it on the kitchen table.
Her little brother Ben accidentally bumped the table while running through the room.
The volcano crashed, and pieces scattered everywhere.
Mina groaned, “My project is ruined!”
Her dad handed her tape and said, “You can’t cry over spilled milk.”
Mina realized she needed to stop worrying about the accident and focus on fixing the problem.
She repaired the volcano as best she could.
It wasn’t perfect, but it still erupted bright orange foam during judging.
activities.hint: The sentence right after the adage usually tells you what it did.

questions.ask: What does “You can’t cry over spilled milk” mean in the passage?

checks.label: Says the thing has already happened
Says being upset does not help

questions.model: It means there is no point being upset about something that has already happened, because you cannot change it.

questions.ask: Which sentence BEST helps a reader understand what the adage means?
questions.answer: Mina realized she needed to stop worrying about the accident and focus on fixing the problem.
options: The volcano crashed, and pieces scattered everywhere.
Mina realized she needed to stop worrying about the accident and focus on fixing the problem.
She repaired the volcano as best she could.

questions.ask: Finish the sentence: Mina’s dad most likely used the adage to…

checks.label: Says what he wanted her to do
Mentions the feeling he was answering

questions.model: encourage Mina to focus on fixing the problem instead of feeling upset

sentences: During lunch, Jordan noticed a container labeled DO NOT OPEN sitting alone on the cafeteria table.
Curious about what was inside, he slowly lifted the lid.
Inside was a tuna sandwich and a banana covered in peanut butter.
At that moment, the owner walked over and frowned.
Mia laughed and said, “Curiosity killed the cat.”
Jordan quickly closed the container and decided some mysteries should stay mysteries.
activities.hint: What happened to Jordan right after he got curious?

questions.ask: What does the adage “Curiosity killed the cat” mean in this passage?
questions.model: It means being too curious about something that is not yours can get you into trouble.

activities.brief: Each cat agent explains an adage. Say whether the explanation is right.
activities.hint: Read the explanation on its own. Does it actually say what the adage says?

items.given: “Actions speak louder than words.” — People’s behavior shows more than what they say.  →  ____
“Don’t judge a book by its cover.” — Books with nice covers are usually interesting.  →  ____
“The early bird catches the worm.” — People who prepare early often have an advantage.  →  ____
“Practice makes perfect.” — Only talented people become successful.  →  ____

activities.brief: Each correct cat agent carries a clue word. The suspect has all of them.
activities.hint: Only the agents who explained their adage correctly count.

items.given: Actions speak louder than words → Backpack.  Don’t judge a book by its cover → Camera.  The early bird catches the worm → Watch.  Practice makes perfect → Sandals.  What is the suspect carrying?  ____

sentences: Kayla had practiced for weeks before the school spelling bee and expected to reach the championship round easily.
However, during the final round, she misspelled a simple word she had reviewed many times before the competition.
Frustrated by her mistake, Kayla told her coach that entering the contest had been a waste of time.
Her coach simply replied, “Every cloud has a silver lining.”
Several days later, Kayla received an email inviting her to join the district vocabulary team based on her earlier performance scores.
Although she still remembered the disappointment of the spelling bee, she began to view the experience differently.
activities.hint: Find the saying first, then work out what it did for Kayla.

questions.ask: Which words in sentence 4 are the adage?
questions.answer: Every cloud has a silver lining
options: Every cloud has a silver lining

questions.ask: What is the meaning of the adage in this paragraph?
questions.answer: Disappointing situations can still lead to something positive.
options: Practicing for competitions always leads to success.
Disappointing situations can still lead to something positive.
Vocabulary teams are harder than spelling bees.
Coaches should encourage students after contests.

core.title: Puns
core.skill: Spotting a word doing two jobs at once, and saying what both are

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions. The sentences are numbered.
sentences: Last Saturday, Andrea helped her Uncle Mateo at his bakery during the town food festival.
Business was slow at first, so her uncle tried using silly jokes to attract customers.
As people walked by, he held up a loaf of bread and shouted, “I loaf making customers smile!”
Then he pointed to a tray of pastries and said, “We always rise to the occasion!”
A few people laughed and stopped at the booth.
Later, when someone asked why the bakery stayed open so late, he replied, “That’s just how we roll.”
Soon, customers crowded around the booth laughing at the jokes while buying cookies, muffins, and warm cinnamon rolls.
activities.hint: A pun is one word doing two jobs. Say both jobs out loud.

questions.ask: Which pun means the baker enjoys making people happy?
options: We always rise to the occasion!

questions.ask: Click the word in sentence 4 that creates the pun, then write the other thing it means.
Why is that pun funny?
questions.model: It is funny because bread dough really does rise, and rising to the occasion also means doing well when something is asked of you.

questions.ask: Why is “That’s just how we roll” a pun?
questions.model: A bakery sells rolls, and “how we roll” is also a saying that means the way we do things.

questions.ask: Which line could the author use in an advertisement for the bakery?
options: “The bakery opens every morning at six.”
“Fresh bread is sold daily at the festival.”
“Customers lined up near the front door.”

activities.brief: A cave, a dragon, and some very bad jokes.
sentences: Liora wandered cautiously through the glowing forest until she discovered a hidden cave behind tangled vines.
Glittering crystals reflected shimmering patterns of light across the rocky floor as she ventured deeper inside.
Soon, she noticed unusual wooden signs hanging beside the tunnels.
One sign pointed toward a rocky passage and read, “This cave is ore-some!”
Another sign beside a pile of gems declared, “You really rock!”
Liora chuckled at the clever signs, but her smile quickly faded when a deep growl echoed through the cavern.
A dragon stepped from the shadows and narrowed its glowing eyes.
“I hope you didn’t take my jokes for granite,” the dragon warned as smoke curled from its nose.
activities.hint: Read the dragon’s line out loud and listen for the word underneath it.

questions.ask: What is the meaning of the pun “This cave is ore-some!”?
questions.answer: The cave is exciting and impressive.
options: The cave is exciting and impressive.
The cave is filled with loud noises.
The cave is dangerous to enter.
The cave is difficult to explore.

questions.ask: Click the pun in the dragon’s warning, then write the word it is playing on.
Explain the dragon’s pun.
questions.model: Granite is a rock found in a cave, and it sounds like granted, so the dragon is asking them not to take its jokes for granted.

activities.brief: One more. Read it, then answer.
sentences: Jordan volunteered at the town garden center during the spring festival.
As he carried pots of colorful flowers to the display tables, the manager smiled and said, “I’m rooting for you today!”
Jordan laughed at the joke and continued helping customers choose plants.
Bright rows of tulips and roses filled the air with a fresh scent.
Later, a customer accidentally knocked over a watering can, spilling water across the floor.
The manager handed her a towel and said, “No need to wet your plants over it!”
The customers chuckled while Jordan realized the manager enjoyed using puns to make people smile.
activities.hint: Roots grow in soil. What else does rooting mean?

questions.ask: Mikey thinks sentence 2 contains a pun. Do you agree?
Explain your reasoning.
questions.model: It is a pun because rooting means cheering someone on, and roots are also part of the plants they sell at the garden centre.

ap_adages.title: SB: Adages
ap_adages.skill: Matching a saying to what it actually means

activities.brief: Read each short story. Choose the meaning of the adage it uses.
activities.hint: Ask what the character did wrong, or did right.

items.given: Mateo carried six heavy boxes at once instead of making two trips, and dropped them all. The coach said, “Slow and steady wins the race.”  →  ____
options: Do not assume success before it happens.
Taking a risk can lead to a reward.

items.given: Ava rushed through her science project the night before it was due, and parts fell apart in class. Her brother said, “Haste makes waste.”  →  ____
options: Do not assume success before it happens.
Taking a risk can lead to a reward.

items.given: Jordan bragged he would win first place at the talent show. His teacher warned, “Don’t count your chickens before they hatch.”  →  ____
items.answer: Do not assume success before it happens.
options: Do not assume success before it happens.
Taking a risk can lead to a reward.

items.given: Leila felt nervous about joining robotics club, went anyway, and made new friends. Her grandmother said, “Nothing ventured, nothing gained.”  →  ____
items.answer: Taking a risk can lead to a reward.
options: Do not assume success before it happens.
Taking a risk can lead to a reward.

sentences: Carter had waited all season for the championship basketball game.
On the morning of the tournament, he packed his water bottle, shoes, and lucky wristband before heading to school.
However, when his team arrived at the gym, Carter realized he had forgotten his basketball jersey at home.
“I can’t believe this happened,” Carter groaned as he searched through his backpack again.
His coach handed him a practice jersey and reminded him, “Look before you leap.”
Coach Daniels explained that Carter had rushed out the door without checking his equipment carefully.
Embarrassed, Carter quickly joined warm-ups and promised himself he would prepare more carefully next time.
activities.hint: The sentence after the adage usually explains it.

questions.ask: Which words in sentence 5 are the adage?
options: His coach handed him a practice jersey

questions.ask: What does that adage mean?
questions.answer: People should think carefully before acting too quickly.
options: Basketball players should always arrive early for games.
People should think carefully before acting too quickly.
Championship games are difficult to prepare for.

sentences: Fiona hurried through the crowded school hallway carrying posters for the student council fundraiser.
Earlier that morning, her teacher had reminded the class, “Better safe than sorry,” but Fiona ignored the advice and stacked too many supplies in her arms at once.
As she rushed toward the cafeteria, several posters slipped onto the floor and scattered everywhere.
Her friend Malik helped gather the papers and reminded her, “Pride comes before a fall.”
Embarrassed, Fiona nodded and carried the remaining supplies more carefully the rest of the afternoon.

questions.ask: Which detail best shows why “Better safe than sorry” applied to Fiona?
questions.answer: She stacked too many supplies in her arms at once.
options: She stacked too many supplies in her arms at once.
She was carrying posters for the fundraiser.

questions.ask: What does the adage “Pride comes before a fall” mean?
questions.model: It means being too proud or too sure of yourself often comes right before you make a mistake.

ap_puns.title: SB: Puns
ap_puns.skill: Telling a pun from an ordinary sentence, one at a time

activities.brief: Does the sentence contain a pun?
activities.hint: A pun has a word doing two jobs. An ordinary sentence does not.

items.given: A baker opens a shop that is rolling in dough.  →  ____
A gardener watered the flowers early every morning.  →  ____
A fisherman opens a seafood restaurant and says the business is off the hook.  →  ____
A cat becomes famous for its purr-fect singing voice.  →  ____
A scientist completed an experiment in the chemistry lab.  →  ____
The sunburned banana said, “I’m peeling terrible today!”  →  ____

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Sean helped his dad at the town bakery during the weekend festival.
As customers lined up for fresh bread, his dad smiled and said, “Business is really rolling today!”
Sean laughed because the word rolling referred to both bread dough and the busy crowd.
Later, a customer asked whether the bakery stayed busy every weekend.
His dad grinned and replied, “We always rise to the occasion.”
Soon, more families gathered around the booth to buy pastries and listen to the bakery jokes.
Sean carried trays of cupcakes to the front table while customers crowded around the bakery booth.
A customer asked if the bakery stayed busy every weekend, and Sean’s dad smiled and said, “Business is really crumby today!”
Sean laughed as more families stopped by to buy desserts and hear the bakery jokes.
activities.hint: Sentence 3 tells you how a pun works. Use the same idea on the others.

questions.ask: Explain what “Business is really rolling today!” means.
questions.model: A bakery rolls dough, and business rolling along also means it is busy and going well.

questions.ask: What is the meaning of the pun in sentence 5?
questions.answer: The phrase refers to bread dough rising and succeeding during challenges.
options: The bakery opens early each morning for customers.
The phrase refers to bread dough rising and succeeding during challenges.
The bakery sells fresh bread during weekend festivals.

questions.ask: Click the word in sentence 8 that creates the pun, then write the word it sounds like.
Explain the pun in sentence 8.
questions.model: Baked goods leave crumbs, and crumby sounds like crummy, which means bad — so it is a joke about business being both.

full.title: Full Topic: Adages & Puns
full.skill: Both skills, in one piece of writing

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Heavy snow covered the sidewalks and roads across Maple Lane.
Mila and her younger brother Theo bundled into thick coats and hurried outside to help shovel the driveway.
As Theo slipped into a snowbank, he laughed, “I guess I really broke the ice today!”
Mila groaned at the joke but helped him back up.
After several minutes of shoveling, Mila complained that clearing the snow would take forever.
Their grandfather smiled and reminded them, “Many hands make light work.”
Soon, several neighbors joined together, passing shovels back and forth while laughing and talking.
activities.hint: One of these is a joke about words. One is a lesson about life.

questions.ask: Which line in the passage is the pun?
questions.answer: I guess I really broke the ice today!
options: I guess I really broke the ice today!
clearing the snow would take forever

questions.ask: Which line in the passage is the adage?
options: I guess I really broke the ice today!

questions.ask: What is the meaning of the pun?
questions.model: Theo really did fall into the ice and snow, and breaking the ice also means starting things off in a friendly way.

questions.ask: What is the meaning of the adage?
questions.model: It means a job gets easier and faster when more people help with it.

questions.ask: Theo says another joke: “Ice to meet this snowstorm!” Click the word in sentence 3 that his new joke plays on, then write the word it sounds like.

activities.brief: A second passage. Same two skills.
sentences: Dark clouds rolled across Cedar Street as rain poured onto the sidewalks and driveways.
Jada and her cousin Marcus hurried outside to help bring in groceries before the storm became worse.
As Marcus slipped while carrying a bag of apples, he laughed and shouted, “Orange you glad I didn’t drop these?”
Jada groaned at the joke but grabbed the bag before it rolled into a puddle.
A few minutes later, the power suddenly went out across the neighborhood.
Jada worried that dinner would be ruined, but her grandmother calmly lit several candles and said, “When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.”
Soon, the family gathered around the kitchen table telling stories and playing card games while rain tapped against the windows.
activities.hint: Say the fruit out loud and listen for the ordinary word inside it.

questions.ask: Click the word that makes Marcus’s joke a pun, then write the word it sounds like.
What is the meaning of that pun?
questions.answer: Marcus uses the word orange to sound like aren’t while joking about the apples.
options: Marcus uses the word orange to sound like aren’t while joking about the apples.
Marcus believes oranges are better than apples.
Marcus wants Jada to buy more fruit from the store.
Marcus thinks the groceries are too heavy to carry.

questions.ask: Explain the meaning of “When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.”
questions.model: It means that when something bad happens you should make the best of it and find something good in it.

sentences: Caleb helped his aunt prepare decorations for the school fundraiser after classes ended.
While they hung colorful banners across the cafeteria, his aunt reminded him, “Don’t put all your eggs in one basket.”
Caleb nodded and continued organizing supplies for different games and activities.
Soon, students arrived with baked goods, raffle prizes, and posters for the event.
Later, one table collapsed, sending markers and papers sliding across the floor.
Caleb quickly helped clean the mess while his aunt smiled proudly at how calmly he handled the problem.
By evening, the fundraiser looked organized and ready to begin.
activities.hint: Is it a saying with a lesson in it, or just an instruction?

questions.ask: Lyla thinks sentence 2 contains an adage. Do you agree?
Explain your reasoning.

checks.label: Says it is an adage or a saying

questions.model: It is an adage because it is a well-known saying that teaches a lesson: do not risk everything on one plan.
